meta.source: The World Atlas of Coffee: From Beans to Brewing — coffees explored, explained and enjoyed (James Hoffmann; Mitchell Beazley)
meta.derivedVia: Distilled notes + pairing heuristics for this app (coffee perception, origins, roast/process); cigar-side rules are application of the book's balance/intensity/harmony principles, not a cigar chapter from the book.
meta.purpose: App-ready data model for a coffee<->cigar pairing engine
meta.note: Attribute coffee knowledge to Hoffmann's atlas. Do not treat cigar pairing scores as verbatim book content. Validate empirically before shipping weight changes.

perceptionFramework.nasalAromas: Complex descriptors (chocolate, berries, caramel) sensed retronasally via olfactory bulb
perceptionFramework.mouthfeel: Physical texture/weight sensed on palate; modeled separately from taste and aroma

acidity.correlations: Higher-density beans and lighter roasts increase acidity; degrades quickly through roast development

sweetness.origin: Fruit ripeness / sugar content of the cherry
sweetness.roastDynamics: Bell curve; peaks between acidity high and bitterness high

bitterness.roastRelationship: Increases roughly linearly with roast time/darkness

qualityMetrics.balance: Whether elements are harmonious or one is 'too loud'
qualityMetrics.aftertaste: Sensation after swallowing; quinic acid -> clean finish; dark fruit/spice may linger by origin
qualityMetrics.complexity: Diversity of flavor layers; higher in high-altitude hand-picked Arabica

arabica.profile: Superior flavor, high acidity & complexity; specialty standard

robusta.profile: Woody/burnt rubber, very low acidity, heavy body, ~2x caffeine

varieties.name: Typica
varieties.notes: Original variety; excellent cup, low yield

varieties.name: Caturra
varieties.notes: Bourbon mutation; quality rises with altitude

varieties.name: Geisha
varieties.notes: Exceptionally aromatic, floral, citrusy; light tea-like body

varieties.name: SL-34
varieties.notes: Similar to SL-28, slightly lower quality

varieties.name: Pacamara
varieties.notes: Large bean; chocolate + fruit, risk of herbal/onion notes

terroirAltitude.terroir: Combined geography + climate effect on flavor
terroirAltitude.altitudeEffect: Higher altitude -> denser beans -> higher acidity + more unusual flavor
terroirAltitude.gradingProxy: Strictly Hard Bean / Strictly High Grown ~ >1200-1300 m (Central America)

processing.washed: Higher acidity, more complexity, clean cup
processing.natural: Adds fruit (blueberry/strawberry/tropical); high body; higher defect risk
processing.semiWashedGilingBasah: Much lower acidity, higher body; wood/earth/spice

roastLevels.light: Preserves acidity, fruit, intrinsic origin flavors
roastLevels.dark: High body & bitterness; acidity lost; generic roast flavor replaces origin

regions.Burundi/Rwanda: Complex berry, juicy acidity, red apple/grape
regions.Brazil: Low acidity, heavy body, very sweet, chocolate/nutty
regions.Indonesia (semi-washed): Heavy-bodied, earthy, woody, spicy; little acidity

matchingDimensions.rule: High TDS (espresso) -> high-intensity partners; low TDS -> lighter partners

complementary.logic: IF Coffee.FlavorFamily == Partner.FlavorFamily AND Coffee.Intensity == Partner.Intensity THEN Compatibility = HIGH

contrasting.description: Use one attribute to refresh/cut through the other
contrasting.example: High-acidity washed Kenya as palate cleanser for heavy earthy partner
contrasting.logic: IF Partner.Body == HEAVY THEN SELECT Coffee.Acidity == HIGH (cleanser) OR Coffee.Sweetness == HIGH (mellowing)

bodyStrengthMatching.rule: Match tactile weight so neither obscures the other
bodyStrengthMatching.lowBodyCoffees: Fully washed/cleaner -> more delicate partners so complexity isn't lost

flavorBridges.mechanism: Inherent tobacco/spice/wood -> complementary to similar profiles
Approachable, sweet, low acidity -> stable partners for sweet profiles
Elegant, tea-like -> require most delicate partners to avoid being overpowered

components.B_bodyMatch: 1.0 if Coffee.Body == Partner.Body exactly; 0.5 if one step apart
components.I_intensityRoastBalance: Higher if Coffee.RoastLevel (bitterness indicator) aligns with partner's perceived strength

scoring.priorityNote: Always match tactile body before flavor notes; a heavy partner drowns a tea-like coffee regardless of flavor similarity
